feature: Shift-click to pick more than one thing on the canvas
summary: Shift-clicking a layer on the picture adds it to what is already picked, and shift-clicking a picked one drops it. Picking exactly two things to group is now two clicks instead of a marquee sweep that takes in whatever else was nearby.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Nothing new to turn on; it rides the same layer groups flag that Group and Ungroup do.

try.do: Draw three rectangles on a blank canvas, spread apart.
Click the top one, then shift-click the middle one.
Press Command G, then Command Z to put it back.
Shift-click the middle one again to drop it, then shift-click the top one to end up with nothing picked.
Pick two, group them, then double-click into the group and shift-click its other piece.
Still inside the group, shift-click the loose rectangle out on the canvas.
Escape twice, sweep a marquee around everything, then shift-click one layer to drop it out of the sweep.

evaluate: Is the dashed outline enough to tell what is picked, or do you want the same handles a single selection gets?
Shift-clicking out on the canvas while you are inside a group does nothing at all. Is that the right answer, or should it pull you out of the group and pick that layer?
When you drop back to one picked layer the handles reappear on it. Does that feel like the right landing point?
Does the last step (dropping one layer out of a marquee sweep) read correctly, with the rubber band coming down as the selection changes?
Would you reach for shift-click before the marquee now, or does the marquee still feel faster for a cluster?
rough: You still cannot DRAG a multi-selection on the canvas: pressing on any picked layer throws the rest away and moves that one alone. That was already true of a marquee selection, but shift-click makes it much easier to walk into. Filed as its own task (drag-a-multi-selection-on-the-canvas-and-everyth).

A shift-click that lands on empty canvas still clears everything, because shift over empty space means constrain-the-band-to-a-square. So a shift-click a few pixels off a layer's edge loses the picking you just did. Filed as its own task (shift-dragging-a-marquee-adds-what-it-sweeps-to).

Fixed along the way: a multi-selection made anywhere but a marquee drew NO outlines on the canvas at all. Shift-clicking in the Layers list highlighted rows and lit up the menus while the picture showed nothing. The outlines used to hang off the marquee's rubber band; now they hang off the selection.
